messages:
Alex R: Hey team — Southbridge reporting sudden p99 spikes on their embeddings route since ~09:10 UTC, p95 fine but p99 up from ~600ms -> ~3.2s. They say it correlates with a recent marketing batch job.
Meera S: ugh okay. Do we have tenant-level throttle kicking in? can you paste the tenant id?
Jordan (CS): Tenant: sb-9876. They started a nightly bulk embed of ~120k items in one job around 09:05. Customer says they used parallel workers at 50 concurrency.
Liz I (Infra): checking metrics now — routing shows sb-9876 hitting sustained concurrency spike; queue depth rose and a number of requests got routed to slower fallback model (quantized-4bit-v2). Also seeing KV cache evictions on the serving hosts pinned to that tenant pool.
sre-bot: Incident hint: noisy-tenant-detection triggered for sb-9876 -> recommend reserve or throttle.
Alex R: Can we confirm if they were on a shared pool or dedicated reservation? Jordan, CS?
Jordan (CS): They are on shared DedicatedPool-3 (reserved by other tenants). No dedicated reservation.
Meera S: Ok immediate mitigation options: 1) apply temporary per-tenant concurrency cap (soft cap 20) + burst reserve 2) apply allowlist for their embed job IPs to route to a larger reserved bucket 3) encourage customer to split job into smaller batches.
Liz I (Infra): I can apply a soft concurrency cap policy on the routing side. Will also enable automatic fallback suppression (so they don't hit slower model variants). Command I'll run: `rwctl route update --tenant sb-9876 --concurrency-cap 20 --suppress-fallback true`
Alex R: Please run it. Jordan, can you message them to pause the job if possible (short window) so infra changes don't disrupt in-flight?
Jordan (CS): pinged them just now: "Hi — we're seeing a noisy concurrent job. Can you pause for ~5-10 min while we apply a temporary cap? We'll follow up with mitigation steps." Their reply: "Pausing now, thx."
Liz I (Infra): Ran command, returns OK. Monitoring.
sre-bot: Policy change applied: concurrency-cap(20) for sb-9876 at host-group dp3-region-us-east. Suppress-fallback enabled.
Meera S: early signs look good — queue depth dropping. p99 back to ~850ms after cap. Still above baseline but much improved.
Alex R: Good. Next: customer asked for a bespoke allowlist so their periodic high-throughput jobs don't get throttled in future. Options: A) dedicated reservation (recommended for predictable throughput) B) allowlist their job runner IPs to route to a high-capacity burst pool C) prebook a temporary reservation for marketing windows.
Jordan (CS): They prefer option B for now — they don't want full reservation. They provided IPs: [203.0.113.45, 203.0.113.46]. Also asked about cost impact.
Liz I (Infra): We can add an IP-based route rule that pins requests from those source IPs to burst-pool-dp3 with higher concurrency and short-lived resource guarantees. I will create a ticket for infra change and put a 72-hour TTL on the rule as requested. Change: `rwctl route add --src-ip 203.0.113.45/32 --tenant sb-9876 --pool burst-pool-dp3 --ttl 72h`
Alex R: Also captured for audit: set request size limits for embeddings to avoid extremely large single requests (their workers were sending 1000 slices per request). Suggest we recommend max 200 per request.
Jordan (CS): Noted. Customer asked for repro steps so they can avoid this: "run smaller batches, add jitter to worker start times, or use the batch-queueing client we provide."
Meera S: Follow-up actions: - infra: apply IP route + create change ticket (Liz) - infra: implement permanent per-tenant reservation proposal if they commit (Liz + Alex) - cs: send playbook to customer with batching guidance and cost estimate (Jordan) - monitoring: add alert for concurrency anomalies per-tenant (Meera)
Liz I (Infra): Created infra change CHG-9912 for allowlist route (scheduled immediate). Also opening a follow-up RFC for tenant reservations sizing.
sre-bot: CHG-9912 deployed: route rule for 203.0.113.45 and 203.0.113.46 added. TTL=72h.
Alex R: Final metrics check at +30m: p95 ~95ms, p99 ~420ms when allowlist active and suppress-fallback true. Queue depth normalized.
Jordan (CS): Customer confirmed resumed job and seeing acceptable latency. They asked for a post-mortem summary and a recommendation to prebook burst windows.
Meera S: I'll own the short post-mortem + add suggested SLO guardrails for batch jobs to our KB.
Alex R: Thanks all. We'll close this thread when post-mortem and KB links posted.
Jordan (CS): adding follow-up: flag for Product to consider "batch-job reservations" UX in console.
Liz I (Infra): Note: we saw KV-cache churn; long-term we'll explore per-tenant cache partitioning to avoid noisy-tenant eviction.
sre-bot: Incident resolved.
